- TEST_SCRIPT.md (168 lines) - a manual QA walkthrough for a feature round that shipped in May 2026 and has since been superseded by content changes.
- STEP_BY_STEP.md (88 lines) - Part 1 was a one-off deploy checklist, now spent. Parts 2-5 are admin how-to (legacy backfill, merge, debt tracking) that duplicates ADMIN_GUIDE's audience, so it folds in there rather than living alone.

- README.md - the door into the repo for anyone landing on it cold.
- ADMIN_GUIDE.md - the manual for Queen Myrtle and Smutley, who are non-technical club admins and will never run Acta.

body:
CORRECTION TO A PRIOR ASSUMPTION: epiClavis has NO SEO or structured-data capability. The doctor --menu capability list confirms it (Acta, Praevisio, Index, Design, Data, Writer - none SEO). The only schema.org text in the whole engine is inside the Merchant INTAKE questionnaire, which asks a new client which schema.org type their business is. That is a client-onboarding question set, not an audit tool, and this project never went through intake. So SEO work here is done by hand.

CURRENT STATE (verified, not assumed):
- index.html already has a strong head: title, description, keywords, geo tags, canonical, full Open Graph and Twitter cards, plus a SportsClub JSON-LD block with sameAs pointing at the club Facebook group.
- api/event.js server-renders every event at /event/:id, fetching it from Supabase and injecting per-event OG/Twitter tags plus the title. It injects NO JSON-LD.
- api/sitemap.js already lists the homepage plus every non-draft event from Supabase.
- robots.txt allows crawling and points at the sitemap. The site is indexable.

THE GAP: every event page is missing Event structured data. This is the single highest-value SEO and agentic-search item on the site, because there are many events and they are exactly the kind of thing an assistant is asked about ("when is the next Sheffield hash run?"). Without it, a crawler or model sees prose it must infer from; with it, the date, place, and status are unambiguous machine-readable fields.

THE APPROACH: emit the JSON-LD from api/event.js, not from event.html. The function ALREADY fetches the event row, so the data is in hand and every event is covered at once with no per-event authoring and nothing for admins to maintain. Crawlers that do not run JavaScript still see it, which client-side injection would not achieve.

title: Event OG/JSON-LD description truncates mid-word at 280 chars (event 18 ends "...to pub." with an unclosed bracket). Truncate at the last word boundary instead
Homepage event lists are client-rendered, so non-JS crawlers see empty grids; consider server-rendering the homepage with ItemList JSON-LD
body:
index.html is a static file: the "Coming up" and "Past Hashes" grids are filled by an inline module script at the bottom of the page, so #events-grid is an empty div in the served HTML. A crawler or AI assistant that does not run JavaScript sees no events on the homepage at all.

This is now PARTLY mitigated: every event has its own server-rendered page at /event/:id carrying full Event JSON-LD (DEC-002), and api/sitemap.js lists all of them, so each hash is independently discoverable. Google also renders JS for indexing, so it likely sees the homepage list. The gap bites hardest for non-rendering agents.

OPTIONS, cheapest first:
1. Add an ItemList JSON-LD block to the homepage listing upcoming events. Would need the homepage to be server-rendered like /event/:id, i.e. a new api/home.js plus a vercel.json rewrite for "/". Moderate change, keeps the static file as the template.
2. Add a <noscript> fallback list. Cheap, but needs the data server-side anyway, so it collapses into option 1.
3. Leave as is and rely on the per-event pages plus the sitemap.

Not urgent, and worth a conversation before doing: option 1 changes how the homepage is served, which touches caching and the deploy shape.

title: Future events missing from "Coming up": two Hash 24 duplicates wrongly marked completed, plus an orphaned past-dated event that shows nowhere
body:
REPORTED AS: "Coming up only shows the latest added event, not all future events."

DIAGNOSIS: the homepage code is CORRECT. The data is wrong. Verified against live Supabase on 2026-09-07.

The homepage runs two queries (index.html around line 640):
  upcoming = event_date >= today AND status != completed  (then filters out 'planning')
  past     = status == completed

Three future-dated events exist, but only ONE reaches "Coming up":

1. DUPLICATE. Hash 24 on 2026-09-19 exists TWICE - id 16 "Steel City H3 19th September 2026 Hash #24" (created 18:22) and id 18 "Steel City H3 Hash 24 Saturday 19th September 2026" (created 18:53), same date, same venue (The Cross Scythes Community Pub), 31 minutes apart. One must be deleted.

2. WRONGLY COMPLETED. BOTH Hash 24 records have status 'completed' with attendance_finalised_at set on 2026-09-06, for an event dated 2026-09-19 that has NOT happened. Neither has a scribe report and written_up is false, so this looks like the admin workflow was clicked through to the end rather than a real finalisation. Because they are 'completed' they fail the upcoming query and are listed under Past Hashes - a future event shown as past.

3. ORPHANED. Event id 15, run #19, "Joint Hash Weekend with Bras & Pants", Buxton, dated 2026-06-27, still has status 'ready'. Its date has passed so it fails the upcoming query, and it is not 'completed' so it fails the past query. It appears NOWHERE on the site.

Fault 3 is a genuine code weakness, not just bad data: ANY event whose date passes without being marked completed silently disappears from the site. The two queries do not cover the whole space. A past-dated event that was never finalised falls through the gap with no warning to anyone.
notes:
[2026-09-07T13:59:51.469Z] The orphaned event turns out to be the club LARGEST event: the Buxton joint weekend with 77 attendees, a GBP 40 per-head residential with meal and accommodation. It had been invisible on the live site since 27 June because its status stayed ready after the date passed. The homepage fix (DEC-003) restores it to the archive. This raises the stakes on the silent-disappearance bug: the event that vanished was the most significant one the club has run.
[2026-09-07T15:19:17.218Z] Hare data from the inspection (2026-09-07): BOTH events 16 and 18 carry the SAME two hares, Smutley (David Smith) and Queen Myrtle (Coleen Trueman), each auto-created within seconds of its event (16 at 18:22:33, 18 at 18:53:45). volunteered=false on all four rows, so both were assigned by an admin rather than someone volunteering. Migration 0009 auto_rsvp_on_hare_insert fires on event_hares INSERT and creates an on_on RSVP for that user, so the 2 RSVPs the guard found on event 16 are near-certainly those same two hares, not real member interest. Conclusion: neither copy holds genuine member data - both are the same shape, created 31 minutes apart. The choice between them is therefore about which TEXT to keep, not which data to preserve.
[2026-09-07T15:21:12.773Z] RESOLUTION AGREED (Adam, 2026-09-07): delete event 16, keep 18. Script rewritten - the old guard aborted on ANY attendance/rsvp/hare rows, which was correct before we had looked but wrong now that we have. New guard checks IDENTITY (right date, right run number) plus a photos check, since a photo is the only irreplaceable thing that could plausibly be on the duplicate. Pre-flight checked against the migrations: run_number is integer, ready exists in the event_status enum, attendance_finalised_at is nullable, updated_at exists, and no BEFORE/AFTER DELETE trigger on events could block the cascade.
[2026-09-07T15:27:25.264Z] RESOLVED on the data side, 2026-09-07. Verified independently against live Supabase: 13 events (was 14), the duplicate id 16 is gone, and id 18 is status ready with attendance_finalised_at null. "Coming up" now returns TWO events (18 on 19 Sep, 17 on 17 Oct) where it previously returned one - the originally reported symptom. Still outstanding: the homepage/event-page code fix (DEC-003) is committed to the working tree but NOT deployed, so the live site will not reflect any of this until it ships.

title: Homepage past-hashes list keys on date passed, not status completed, so an unfinalised past event cannot silently vanish
body:
The homepage past-hashes query keyed on status == 'completed'. Combined with the upcoming query (event_date >= today AND status != completed), that left a hole: an event whose date passed while its status was still 'ready' (or 'open', 'hares_wanted') matched NEITHER query and disappeared from the site with no warning.

This was not hypothetical - event id 15, the Buxton joint hash weekend of 2026-06-27, had been invisible on the live site for over two months. Nobody noticed because a missing row looks the same as a row that was never created.

The fix makes "past" mean what the word means: event_date < today. Whether an admin has got round to finalising the paperwork is a workflow state, not a statement about time. Draft ('planning') and cancelled ('closed') events stay excluded, so the archive still shows only real hashes that actually happened.

renderPastRow already degrades correctly for a non-finalised event: the charity line is gated on attendance_finalised_at, and the write-up/photo tags on their own fields, so an unfinalised past hash renders cleanly without them.

Verified against live data: the archive goes from 10 rows to 11, picking up the Buxton hash. Events 16 and 18 remain hidden, which is correct - that is the separate data fault in ISS-003 (a future-dated hash wrongly marked completed), and only a data fix clears it.

title: Admin event tabs offer no plain Save; the only button on the attendance tab irreversibly completes the event with no confirmation
body:
USER REPORT (Smutley/Queen Myrtle, via Adam): "they couldn't find a save button, so they clicked Save & Complete."

That is a UI fault, not user error. Verified in admin-event.html:

1. EVERY tab has exactly ONE orange button, and three of the four both save AND advance the workflow:
   Tab 1 "Save & invite" (-> emails everyone)   Tab 2 "Save & On-On" (-> status 'ready')
   Tab 3 "Save & complete" (-> status 'completed' + finalises attendance)   Tab 4 "Save write-up" (the only plain save)
   There is NO plain "save" anywhere in the workflow tabs. A cautious user looking to save their work has literally no correct button to press.

2. On tab 3 the button is WORSE THAN UNNECESSARY: every attendance edit already persists immediately (event_attendances update/insert/delete fire per row - lines 1016-1074). Nothing on that tab is unsaved. So the one button offered to a user who wants to "save" does nothing they need and irreversibly completes the event.

3. saveComplete() (line 757) has NO confirmation step. One click sets status='completed' AND stamps attendance_finalised_at. It does not check whether the event date has even passed.

4. It is IRREVERSIBLE from the UI. There is no un-complete control anywhere, which is why the bad state needed a manual database fix.

CONSEQUENCE: two future-dated Hash 24 records marked completed+finalised on 2026-09-06 for an event on 2026-09-19 (ISS-003).

FIXES: (a) add a real plain Save on every tab, (b) make advancing the workflow a separate, clearly-labelled, confirmed action, (c) refuse/warn when completing an event whose date has not passed, (d) give admins a roll-back so a mistake is self-serviceable, (e) far more help text - these are non-technical volunteers.
notes: [2026-09-07T15:37:46.078Z] PASS 1 landed 2026-09-07: tabs unlocked (no navigation requires a state change), plain Save added to the attendance and hares tabs, completing now goes through a confirmation that names its three consequences and shouts if the date has not passed, and admins can re-open a completed hash themselves. Verified: the exact Hash 24 case (12 days in the future) now triggers the red warning. PASS 2 still open - modal shell, focus-driven help panel, help text for 23 fields, bulk-add attendees.

title: Full redesign of the admin event workflow, not just guard rails
body:
Adam chose a FULL REDESIGN of the admin event workflow (over the cheaper guard-rails-only option), 2026-09-07, after Smutley/Queen Myrtle marked a future hash complete because "they couldn't find a save button, so they clicked Save & Complete".

THE REAL PROBLEM, stated plainly: the four-tab workflow encodes the DEVELOPER's model of an event's lifecycle (planning -> hares -> open -> ready -> completed) and asks volunteers to drive it. They use it a few times a month, so they never build fluency. Every tab's single orange button both saves AND advances a state machine they cannot see, and no tab offers a plain save. The interface never shows where you are, what happens next, or how to undo.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES for the rework:
1. SAVING IS NEVER A DECISION. A plain Save on every tab that only saves. Advancing the workflow is always a separate, deliberately-styled action.
2. NOTHING IRREVERSIBLE WITHOUT CONFIRMATION, and nothing irreversible full stop. Completing an event must confirm, must say what it will do in plain words, and must warn hard when the date has not passed. Every state change gets a roll-back an admin can perform themselves.
3. SHOW THE STATE. The admin should always see which stage the hash is at, what that means, and what the next step is - not infer it from which tab is green.
4. WRITE FOR A VOLUNTEER, NOT A DEVELOPER. Help text on every control, in club language. "Mark this hash complete" not "set status". Say the consequence: "closes RSVPs and files it in the archive".
5. THE COMMON PATH SHOULD BE OBVIOUS AND THE RARE PATH FINDABLE. Most sessions are: check who's coming, take the money, done.

KNOWN SPECIFICS TO FIX (from ISS-004):
- Tab 3's attendance edits already save instantly per row, so its "Save & complete" button is worse than useless: it offers to "save" something with nothing unsaved, and irreversibly completes instead.
- saveComplete() has no confirmation and no date check.
- No un-complete control exists anywhere, which is why this needed a manual database fix (supabase/fixes/2026-09-07_hash24_duplicate.sql).
- Bulk entry is missing: adding 77 legacy attendees one at a time is not viable, and that is a real request.

STILL TO DECIDE before building: whether the four-tab shape survives at all, or whether this becomes a single scrolling page with a status header. Worth watching an admin use it before committing.

title: Admin event editing moves into a modal with four tabs, a focus-driven help panel, consequence-stating stage transitions, and admin-performable roll-back
body:
Adam's brief, 2026-09-07, in his own terms:

CONTEXT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING: "they are not going to be entering information frequently... using it once a month to add new hashes". Monthly use means NO FLUENCY IS EVER BUILT - every visit is effectively a first visit. Design for someone who has never seen the screen, every single time. They are also Adam's family, which he states directly as the reason to go the extra mile: "they are my family, so going the extra effort to make it crystal clear what each field needs".

WHAT HE ASKED FOR:
1. MODAL, NOT IN-PAGE. Add/edit a hash in a pop-up modal rather than the current in-page form. Focuses attention on one task; the page behind stays as context.
2. KEEP THE FOUR TABS, inside the modal.
3. FIELD-LEVEL HELP ON FOCUS. When a field is selected, a help section shows explicit text covering THREE things: what the field is, what to put in it, and WHAT IT AFFECTS. That third one is the part currently missing everywhere - a volunteer cannot see that "status" silently controls whether the hash appears on the homepage.
4. STAGE TRANSITIONS MUST STATE THEIR CONSEQUENCES. "To move to the next stage it should be clear what moving to the next step means." Not a generic confirm - name what will happen: who gets emailed, whether RSVPs close, whether it leaves the Coming-up list.
5. ROLL-BACK. Confirmed. Every stage change must be undoable by the admins themselves, without Adam or a database fix.

DESIGN CONSEQUENCES I'd draw from that brief:
- Help text is the PRIMARY content of this UI, not decoration. Budget layout space for it from the start rather than bolting hints on.
- One help panel that updates on focus beats 30 tooltips: tooltips need discovery and hover, which fails on touch and rewards fluency the users will never have.
- Never let a stage change be the only button on a screen (that is exactly what caused ISS-004).
- Plain Save must exist and be visually distinct from Advance, everywhere.
- The date check on completing is non-negotiable: warn loudly when completing a hash whose date has not passed.
- Say what a stage MEANS in club language on the screen, not just its name: "Ready to on-on - RSVPs open, everyone can see it on the homepage".

STILL UNKNOWN, worth asking before building: whether they work on a laptop after the hash or a phone at the pub (drives modal sizing and touch targets), and whether the two of them split the work (one does money, one does the write-up).

title: Admin event modal is designed desktop-first for laptop use, which makes a persistent side-by-side help panel affordable
body:
Adam, 2026-09-07: "Laptop after the hash, they'd never do it at the pub."

WHAT THIS SETTLES:
- The event modal is designed DESKTOP-FIRST. It can be wide, which is what makes the always-visible help panel affordable: a two-column modal (form left, help right) works on a laptop and would be impossible on a phone.
- Help text can be a persistent PANEL rather than tooltips or expandable hints. There is room to show it permanently, so the user never has to discover it. This is the single biggest win available and it depends entirely on the laptop assumption.
- Keyboard is available: tab-through field order matters, focus drives the help panel naturally, and Escape/Enter behave conventionally. On a phone, focus-driven help would be hidden behind the on-screen keyboard.
- Touch-target sizing is NOT the constraint. Legibility and explicitness are.
- Mobile still must not BREAK (someone will open it on a phone eventually), but it is the fallback, not the target: the help panel can collapse under the form rather than sitting beside it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE: everything still has to work for someone who has not seen the screen for a month.

REUSE, NOT REINVENT: spice.css already has a .modal-overlay / .modal pattern (line 2383) used for type-to-confirm destructive actions - cream panel, 4px ink border, 10px orange offset shadow, max-width 480px. The event modal should EXTEND this pattern with a wider variant rather than introducing a second modal language. The existing type-to-confirm modal is also the natural model for the stage-transition confirmations (TODO-040).

title: Tabs are locked by event status, so advancing the status is the only way to reach a later tab - navigation requires a destructive state change
body:
Adam, 2026-09-07: the admin work is shared "between the two of them" (Smutley and Queen Myrtle) rather than owned per-person.

THIS BREAKS THE CURRENT DESIGN, and explains the ISS-004 incident more completely than "they could not find Save".

tabsForStatus() (admin-event.html:459) LOCKS tabs by status:
  planning              -> only 'details'
  hares_wanted/open/closed -> 'details' + 'whos'
  ready/completed       -> all four
So the "After the event" (write-up) tab is UNREACHABLE until the event is 'ready' or 'completed'. applyStatusUI() sets t.disabled = true and adds .locked, and the click handler (line 1185) ignores disabled tabs.

CONSEQUENCE: if either of them wanted to get to a later tab, the ONLY way to unlock it was to ADVANCE THE STATUS. "Save & complete" was not merely the nearest button - it was the only route to the part of the form they wanted. The gating turned a destructive state change into a navigation control.

WHY SHARED WORK MAKES THIS WORSE: with two people working on the same hash at different times, neither knows what stage the other left it at. One opens it to add the write-up, finds that tab greyed out, and the interface offers exactly one way forward. There is no "I just want to look at that bit" path.

DESIGN CONSEQUENCES:
1. NAVIGATION MUST NEVER REQUIRE A STATE CHANGE. Every tab should be reachable, always. A tab that is not yet relevant can say so ("nothing to write up until the hash has happened") while still being READABLE. Show, do not lock.
2. If a control must stay disabled, it is the individual SAVE inside that tab - never the tab itself.
3. Because either of them may pick up any part, each tab has to be self-explanatory standing alone: what this step is for, whether it still needs doing, and who did what last. Do not assume the reader has just done the previous tab.
4. Consider showing WHO last changed something and WHEN. With two people sharing, "Queen Myrtle updated the money on 3 June" prevents duplicated or contradictory work. admin_actions already exists (migration 0005) as an audit trail to source this from.

title: Unlock all four tabs: make every tab reachable regardless of status, showing "not yet relevant" copy instead of disabling
Surface "who changed what, when" on the event modal from the existing admin_actions audit trail, so two people sharing the work do not duplicate or contradict each other
Make each tab self-explanatory standing alone - what the step is for and whether it still needs doing - since either admin may pick up any part
Roll-back preserves all entered data and view state, but the modal states the two real side effects (debt visibility, charity total) rather than claiming it is consequence-free
body:
Adam asked whether roll-back is seamless and whether it preserves data entered on later tabs. Traced it properly rather than assuming.

WHAT RE-OPENING ACTUALLY WRITES: setEventStatus('ready', { attendance_finalised_at: null }) - exactly two columns on events. Nothing else is touched, and there is no ON UPDATE trigger that cascades. So every attendance row, payment tick, the scribe report, written_up, photos, hares and RSVPs survive untouched. The write-up tab is fully independent: saveAfter() writes its own columns directly and never reads status, so it stays editable throughout.

VIEW STATE: doReopen() deliberately does NOT call showTab(), so the admin stays on the tab they were on. setupAttendance() admits both 'ready' and 'completed', so the roster keeps working after the rollback rather than emptying. That is the seamlessness Adam asked for.

BUT IT IS NOT CONSEQUENCE-FREE, and the first version of the modal wrongly implied it was. Clearing attendance_finalised_at reaches beyond this tab, because two things key off it:
  - DEBT TRACKING (migration 0018, get_member_debts + the owes-money badges): counts only events where attendance_finalised_at is not null. Re-opening makes anyone who owes for that hash stop showing as owing it.
  - CHARITY TOTAL (migration 0012, get_charity_totals): sums charity_raised across finalised events only, so re-opening a charity hash temporarily reduces the public homepage counter.
Both reverse completely on re-completing; nothing is deleted at any point.

DECISION: say so in the modal rather than reassure. The re-open dialog now leads with "Nothing you've typed is lost", then lists what genuinely changes while it is open, and closes by saying both effects come straight back. The debt line is computed from the actual roster (hidden entirely when nobody owes, and singular/plural correct), and the charity line only appears for a charity hash that actually raised something. A warning that lists consequences which do not apply teaches people to ignore warnings.

title: Event editor opens as an iframe modal over the events list, keeping one editor at one URL rather than duplicating the form
body:
Adam, 2026-09-07: "Open it over the events list, never leave Manage Events."

IMPLEMENTED AS AN IFRAME, not a copy of the form. admin-event.html is 1,477 lines and is linked from FIVE other places: admin-events.html (3 links), admin.html (4), event.html (the public page's edit pencil), admin-attendance.html, and index.html. Duplicating the editor into the list page would guarantee the two drift apart, and would leave the other five entry points on the old one. The iframe keeps ONE editor at ONE URL that works standalone and embedded.

HOW IT HANGS TOGETHER:
- The list intercepts clicks on any a[href^="/admin-event.html"] and opens the modal instead. The real href stays in the markup, so it still works with JS off and ctrl/cmd/shift-click still opens a new tab (explicitly checked for).
- ?embed=1 tells the editor it is inside the modal. It adds .embedded to <html>, and CSS hides the site header, breadcrumb subbar and footer - the shell already provides the frame and the way out. Standalone visits are untouched.
- The editor posts {sch3:'saved'} to the parent on every write (setEventStatus covers all status changes; the three direct saves are hooked individually). The list sets a dirty flag and re-runs its load on close, so a changed status/money/write-up flag is reflected in the row behind.
- {sch3:'close'} handles the two cases where the editor would otherwise navigate: after a DELETE (which redirected to admin-events.html and would have nested the whole admin page inside the frame), and any "Back to events"/"Cancel" link. Both are intercepted in embed mode.
- Creating a new event still redirects to itself with the real id, now carrying embed=1 so the chrome does not reappear mid-flow.
- postMessage is origin-checked on both sides.

VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER (static harness reproducing the shell + a stub editor, since admin auth cannot be reached on localhost - the magic-link redirect is not allow-listed for localhost). Confirmed: opening does not navigate; the row title becomes the modal heading; background scroll locks and restores; the embedded page's header/subbar/footer compute to display:none; save marks dirty; Escape, the Close button, the backdrop and the in-frame back link all close correctly; and the shell centres with room for the offset shadow (gaps 173/173 and 47/48).

DESKTOP-FIRST per DEC-006: 1180x920 capped to the viewport, going full-bleed under 900px so it still works on a phone without being designed for one.

title: Editor is redesigned help-first for two named elderly users: explanation is the primary content, fields are low-density, and each stage carries a plain-English status explanation
body:
Adam, 2026-09-07, describing what he actually wants from the editor:

"Imagine a large off-white dialog box, that carefully walks through each feature. We can then have fewer visible fields... It should be almost help-text orientated rather than field-orientated... It is not general good UI design, but custom built for a seventy year old, that was tech savvy ten years ago and a 65 year old, who has never been particularly tech savvy. UI for OAPs."

THE INVERSION. What exists now is A FORM WITH HELP ATTACHED. What he wants is HELP WITH FIELDS ATTACHED. That is not a styling change, it is a different information hierarchy:
- The explanation is the primary content of the screen; the input is the thing you do once you have read it.
- FEWER FIELDS VISIBLE AT ONCE. Deliberately low density, scrolling to reach the rest. Density is the enemy here: a wall of 18 inputs is where a non-technical user freezes.
- Help text sits WITH its field and is specific to it - not a generic hint, but what this box is, what to type, and what it will change.
- A FIXED STATUS EXPLANATION anchoring each stage in plain sentences: "You are READY TO ON-ON. This means you have set the event up and sent..." Grounding, not decoration - a volunteer who opens this once a month has no idea where in the process they are.

WHY THIS OVERRIDES CONVENTIONAL PRACTICE. Two named users, both retired, one formerly tech-savvy and one never. There is no cohort to generalise across and no fluency to build on: they use it once a month, so every visit is a first visit. Optimising for information density, expert speed or "clean" minimal chrome would be optimising for users this product does not have. Verbosity that would be patronising in a consumer app is exactly right here.

WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES: DEC-005's side-panel-beside-the-form arrangement. The help CONTENT written for all 23 fields (TODO-039) is still good and carries over - it is the layout and hierarchy that change. Adam confirmed he likes the permanent panel and its content; the problem is that the bright panel and the form compete, so nothing signals where the work happens.

title: Editor gets a frozen header (name with inline edit, status, chevron tabs) and two-column field/help layout; conventional styling inside the editor
body:
Adam, 2026-09-07, revising the editor layout again. "Break design convention to make this practical."

THE FROZEN HEADER, three bands that never scroll away:
1. Modal title bar: "Edit Event" left, STATUS chip right.
2. The EVENT NAME as the modal title, with a PENCIL ICON beside it so the name can be edited from any tab without going back to tab 1.
3. The status description underneath (where you are / what it means / what next), small text, frozen.
4. The TABS, also frozen, redrawn as CHEVRONS pointing at the next step so the workflow direction is visible rather than implied.
Together these anchor identity (what am I editing), state (where is it up to) and navigation (what comes next) permanently on screen. A volunteer who scrolls halfway down a long form currently loses all three.

THE FIELD LAYOUT INVERTS AGAIN: fields LEFT, help text RIGHT, in parallel columns.
Adam's reasoning, which is better than my inline version: "There are some fields that they will get used to and breeze through, so the help text is easier to ignore, yet for when they have a memory lapse they can always refer to the help text."
That is the crucial point I got wrong. Help stacked UNDER each field forces everyone to read past it forever, including on the fields they now know cold. A parallel column is IGNORABLE BY DEFAULT and available on demand - it rewards growing familiarity instead of punishing it. It also fits more fields on screen, which addresses the excessive scrolling the inline version introduced.
Note this is NOT a return to the single floating side panel (DEC-005): that was ONE panel for the whole form, competing with it. This is per-field help sitting beside its own field, so the pairing is unambiguous.

VISUAL DIRECTION: "let's make this bit look a lot more conventional for them." The Spice & Steel comic styling (Bangers display type, heavy borders, offset shadows) is right for the public site and actively unhelpful in a data-entry form used by two people in their 60s and 70s. Keep some colouration for continuity; drop the theatrics inside the editor. Plainer type, calmer borders, ordinary form conventions they will recognise from every other website they have used.

SUPERSEDES the inline-help layout of DEC-009. The help COPY and the status explainer content both carry over unchanged; DEC-009's principle (help-first, low density, plain language, built for two named users) still holds - this is a better execution of it.

title: Act on Smutley and Queen Myrtle feedback on the redesigned event editor - paused 2026-09-07 awaiting their use of it
body: The editor redesign is live and deliberately parked here rather than iterating further without real use. Adam: "there is probably more we can do, but it is easier to navigate for my elderly dependents. I will await more feedback before making any further changes." WHAT TO ASK THEM: does the frozen status description tell them what they need at a glance; do they use the help column or ignore it (both are fine - it is designed to be ignorable); does the club language read right or does it sound like an outsider wrote it (the part Claude is least confident in - phrases like "on-inn pub" and "hares and first-timers go free" were inferred from the code); is the scrolling now too long with one field per row. WATCHING ONE OF THEM USE IT (TODO-035) remains the highest-value next step - the original bug was invisible in the code and obvious in one sentence of theirs.

title: Event pages served mojibake: res.end(string) re-encoded UTF-8, so middle dots and em dashes rendered as broken characters in the JSON-LD name and link previews
body: Found while checking why Search Console showed no Events report. The structured data was correct and complete, but every non-ASCII character in it was double-encoded on the way out: "·" became "Â·" and "—" became "â€". Cause: api/event.js passed the HTML string to res.end(), and the runtime re-encoded it rather than writing the UTF-8 bytes. Both readFileSync(utf8) and the charset header were already correct, which is what made it non-obvious. Fixed by writing an explicit Buffer.from(html, "utf8") with a matching content-length. Verified: byte length now exceeds character length (56103 vs 55850) and all 13 events produce clean JSON-LD. api/sitemap.js emits only URLs and dates so it was never affected.

value: Member portal + public site for Steel City H3, Sheffield hash house harriers club. Plain static HTML/CSS/vanilla JS (no build step), deployed on Vercel, backed by Supabase (auth via email OTP, Postgres with RLS, Storage for event photos, edge functions). Live on real club data since 2026-05-22. Public pages show upcoming/past hashes; an admin area runs a 4-tab event workflow (details, who is coming, ready to on-on, after the event) covering RSVPs, hares, attendance, money and write-ups.

Two audiences: the public/prospective hashers browsing upcoming runs and club info, and club members plus a small non-technical mismanagement team (Smutley, Queen Myrtle) who run events through the admin UI. Admins are not technical, so admin screens must be self-explanatory.

Spice and Steel design system: cream Hendersons-Relish-buff backgrounds, Sheffield-steel grey accents, hot-orange highlights, Beano-style comic display type (Bangers, Lilita One, Nunito, Caveat for handwritten captions). Single theme, no dark mode planned. All styles live in one hand-maintained spice.css.

No build step and no package.json by design - the site must stay openable as plain files. MCP cannot reach this Supabase project, so Adam runs all SQL migrations by hand. Commit and push only when Adam asks. The GBP3 hash subs are club funds, not charity; first hash is free. INDEXING: inline <script> blocks inside .html files ARE now indexed - run extract-html.cjs (638 symbols, 1065 class usages from 19 files); this closed the long-standing blind spot where table "used by" counts read as zero. Planned but not started: the email and audience phase (about 200 imported contacts, event invites, newsletters, magic-link RSVP).
